title: Two K-flat resolutions: augmentation square computing the derived-to-ordinary tensor comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], and total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $L,M$ be module sheaves, and let $q:P\to L[0]$ and $\epsilon:C\to M[0]$ be quasi-isomorphisms with $P,C$ bounded above, termwise flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. There is a commuting square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}P\otimes_R C&\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon}&P\otimes_R M[0]\\ q\otimes1\downarrow&&\downarrow q\otimes1\\ L[0]\otimes_R C&\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon}&(L\otimes_R M)[0].\end{array}$$
The top and left arrows are quasi-isomorphisms. With $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(d_Yy+f(x),-d_Xx)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], their cones are naturally isomorphic to $\operatorname{Cone}(\epsilon)\otimes_R P$ and $\operatorname{Cone}(q)\otimes_R C$, respectively, using the Koszul symmetry. Under the derived tensor model [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], the right arrow represents the canonical derived-to-ordinary comparison $L\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}M\to(L\otimes_R M)[0]$. If the bottom arrow is a quasi-isomorphism, that comparison is an isomorphism. These identifications commute with morphisms of the two augmented resolutions.

proof.text: The two composites around the displayed square agree by bifunctoriality: both are q tensor epsilon. The target is (L tensor M)[0] since only degree zero survives. For later use, the Koszul symmetry on homogeneous local tensors is x tensor y ↦ (-1)^{ij} y tensor x for degrees i,j. With the total differential in the cited definition, both d followed by symmetry and symmetry followed by d have coefficients (-1)^{ij+j} on y tensor dx and (-1)^{ij} on dy tensor x. Thus this is a chain map; its square is the identity and its formula commutes with degree-preserving maps. These local balanced formulas induce the claimed natural symmetry of the sheaf total tensors.

source.place: Tag 06YM (lemma-derived-tor-exact), total tensor; the explicit symmetry calculation uses its signed total differential

proof.text: The cones of epsilon and q are acyclic by the cone criterion. The defining K-flat condition applied to the acyclic complex Cone(epsilon) and K-flat factor P makes Tot(Cone(epsilon) tensor P) acyclic. Applied to Cone(q) and K-flat factor C it makes Tot(Cone(q) tensor C) acyclic. In both applications the K-flat factor is on the right, exactly as required by the definition.

The natural tensor-cone comparison identifies Tot(P tensor Cone(epsilon)) with Cone(1 tensor epsilon), compatibly with the cone inclusion. Applying the Koszul sign symmetry gives the stated identification with Cone(epsilon) tensor P. The same comparison applied after symmetry identifies Cone(q tensor 1) with Cone(q) tensor C. Transporting the acyclicity from step 2 across these isomorphisms and applying the cone criterion proves that the top and left arrows are quasi-isomorphisms.

proof.text: The augmentation square is natural in P, C, q, and epsilon: a morphism of augmented resolutions commutes with each tensor factor, with q and epsilon, and hence with the four square maps. The cone comparisons are natural because the tensor-cone isomorphism and the Koszul symmetry are natural chain isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06YM, naturality of the tensor construction and cone maps

proof.text: The natural representative comparison rho is supplied in the theorem hypotheses. Compose its component with T applied to the quasi-isomorphisms Q(q), Q(epsilon) to obtain the representative isomorphism. Invert the image of the top arrow and compose with this representative to define e. Functoriality cancels the top arrow against the full augmentation, giving precisely the stated comparison normalization. Naturality of rho, the commuting augmentation squares and the degree-zero tensor identification give naturality of e and comparison.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YU and 06YM, derived tensor computed by K-flat representatives

proof.text: Suppose the bottom arrow d is a quasi-isomorphism. For every degree n the commuting square gives H^n(c) H^n(a) = H^n(d) H^n(b). The three maps H^n(a), H^n(b), H^n(d) are invertible, by step 3 and the extra hypothesis. Hence H^n(c) = H^n(d) H^n(b) H^n(a)^{-1} is invertible. By the definition of quasi-isomorphism c is a quasi-isomorphism, so its image under the derived-category localization is invertible. Step 5 identifies that image with the canonical comparison in the stated model.
